# Native debrid providers

A hosted source plugin may declare `debrid_provider` and
`ether.contributes.source.class: "debrid"`. Its account belongs in secret settings,
read with `ether.secret.get`. It registers automatically with the native debrid
pipeline while enabled; disabling or removing the plugin unregisters it.

The host sends JSON POST requests to these routes:

| Route under `/ether/debrid/` | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | `{hashes: string[]}` | `{cached: Record<string, boolean>}` |
| `find` | `{infoHash}` | `{torrentId}` |
| `acquire` | `{infoHash, magnet, torrentId, cachedOnly}` | `{torrentId, ready, added, files: [{id, path, size, link?}]}` |
| `link` | `{torrentId, fileId, path, link, magnet, infoHash, size}` | `{url, size, expires?}` |
| `remove` | `{torrentId}` | `{}` |
| `account` | `{}` | `{user, premium, expires?}` |

Times are RFC3339. File sizes are bytes. `added` must be true only when this
request created the provider torrent. The host selects the movie or episode
from `files`; it never sends executable selection callbacks to a plugin.
Unready acquisitions become cache misses. Cleanup only applies to newly added
torrents when the caller's removal policy permits it. A cached-only service may
return HTTP 501 for `find` and `remove`.

HTTP 401/403 means invalid credentials, 404/410 gone, 409 not cached, 429 rate
limited, and 501 unsupported. Other failures use a generic provider error.
Plugin links must be public HTTP(S) URLs; both link validation and every network
dial/redirect use the guarded transport. Native retry, cache, limiter and file
selection behavior applies. Plugin providers currently run after configured
built-in providers at priority 1000; source-card display order does not change
that priority.

Provide `/ether/health` with `status: "attention"` and a useful `reason` when
credentials are absent. `/ether/test` should verify the account and return
`{ok, message}` without exposing credentials or signed URLs. Offline installation
checks cannot establish that a paid account works; test it after setup.

# Plugin content kinds

A content plugin adds a whole **library** to Ether — audiobooks,
comics, music, books, photos, field recordings, anything flat or
hierarchical — with no core changes. The owner meets each kind you
declare as a library beside Movies and TV Shows, in the console and
in every client app you publish it to.

This page is the contract. The worked example is
[`sdk/examples/kind-library`](../sdk/examples/kind-library); the
Studio "A new library" template generates the same skeleton from a
description.

## Declare a kind

In the manifest's `ether` block: `kind: "content"`, at least one of
the `catalog_provider` / `kind_resolver` capabilities (plus optional
`matcher` and `frontend_adapter`), and one entry per kind in
`contributes.mediaKinds`:

```jsonc
{
  "key": "recordings",              // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$, unique in the plugin
  "label": "Field recordings",
  "library": { "name": "Field Recordings" },   // default name; the owner can rename
  "levels": [                       // 1–5 levels, first is the root
    { "key": "collection", "label": "Collection" },
    { "key": "album", "label": "Album", "container": true },
    { "key": "track", "label": "Track", "playable": true }
  ],
  "fields": [                       // validated per item; indexed ones can facet
    { "key": "genre", "type": "string", "label": "Genre", "indexed": true },
    { "key": "durationSec", "type": "duration", "label": "Duration" }
  ],
  "present": { /* see "Publishing" */ },
  "browse": { "sorts": ["title", "index"], "facets": ["genre"], "search": true, "liveSearch": true },
  "sync": { "mode": "pull", "refresh": "1h" },
  "cache": { "maxBytes": 2147483648 },        // optional; per-library blob cache
  "match": { "thresholdDefault": 0.8 }        // optional
}
```

Rules that will bite if ignored: at least one level must be
`playable`; facet fields must be `indexed`; field keys may not reuse
envelope names (`id`, `title`, …); declarations are **additive across
versions** — removing or retyping a field/level is refused at upgrade
unless the owner agrees to replace the library's contents.

## The item envelope

Your provider returns `KindItem`s: your own `id` (letters, digits,
`. _ ~ -`, ≤128 chars — Ether namespaces it, you never see the stored
identity), `level`, `parentId`, `index` within the parent, `title`,
optional `summary/year/released/rating`, `playable`, counts, `art`
(`poster/backdrop/thumb/logo` plus declared roles), `fields` (checked
against your declaration; unknown keys are dropped, wrong types
reject the item), `hints` (an opaque JSON object ≤16 KiB, stored and
handed back to your resolver verbatim — put ids and locators there,
never secrets), and an `etag` for cheap re-syncs.

Caps: title 500 characters, summary 20k, each field 4k, 16 art roles.

## Routes Ether calls

Kind and setup routes are `GET`/`POST` with JSON in and out, through the
normal plugin transport. Frontend-adapter traffic keeps whatever method and
query the client sent:

| Route | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/browse` | Pull sync walks your catalogue | One level per call (`parentId`, `level`, `cursor`, `limit`). Return `nextCursor` or the full set up to `limit`; never more than `limit` items. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/changes` | Pull sync refresh | Optional delta feed `{upserts, deletes, nextCursor, complete}`. Answer 404/501 and Ether re-walks and diffs by `etag` instead. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/items/{id}` | Conformance and detail refresh | One full item. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/search` | Client searches, only when `browse.liveSearch` is on | Same page shape as browse with `query` set. Short budget; see below. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/resolve` | A viewer presses play | `{libraryKey, item, partIndex?, client?}` → ordered `sources`. Never called during browse. |
| `/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/match` | Resolve-time matching, console re-match | `{item, candidates}` → `{matches:[{candidateRef, score 0..1, reasons}]}` best first. |
| `/ether/v1/setup/{step}/test` | The setup wizard | `{step, fields}` → `{ok, detail, fields?}`. Secrets arrive via `SecretGet`, never in this body. |
| `/ether/v1/frontend/{key}/…` | Your frontend adapter's traffic | Any method, and the original query string (repeated keys flatten to the first value). Ether authenticated the viewer first; you get `X-Ether-Viewer` headers, never a credential. |

Clients are **always served from Ether's store** — browse, search
and detail never call you live, so nothing scales with your catalogue
size. You are called at sync time and at play time.

Sync modes: **pull** (Ether walks `browse`, then polls `changes` on
your `refresh`, minimum 15m) or **push** (you call the `KindUpsert`
host service; refused for pull kinds — one writer per kind). A pull
walk that would delete more than half the library aborts and raises
owner attention instead of wiping it.

### Live search

With `browse.liveSearch: true`, a client search on your library also
calls your `/search` route with a short budget (about two seconds).
Results are validated, **upserted into the store like synced items**
(stubs are fine — playable leaves resolve at play time), and merged
with local results. On timeout or error the viewer gets local
results in time and your late answer still lands in the store for
the next search. Declare it only if your source can answer a search
quickly; the Studio template has it on with the explanation beside
the toggle. Pair it with `browse.search: true` so earlier live
results stay findable locally.

## Resolving bytes

`resolve` returns ordered `PlayableSource`s; Ether tries them in
order. Patterns:

- **file** — a hosted resolver path inside an owner-picked folder; requires
  `folders: read` and live containment checks when resolving and opening.
- **range** — a URL Ether reads with HTTP Range (demoted to download
  when the host cannot range and the size fits the cache).
- **download** — fetched whole into the per-library blob cache
  (SHA-256 checked when you provide one), then served locally.
- **direct** — the client surface is handed the URL (only where the
  surface supports it).
- **container** — one member of a zip/RAR/7z, possibly multi-volume:
  `{volumes:[{url,size}], member}` or `memberIndex`. Passwords come
  from a named settings secret (`passwordSecret`), never from your
  response. Ether caches the extracted member.
- **release** — hand Ether a magnet/infohash/NZB and its existing
  debrid/Usenet/torrent pipeline opens it.

URLs may carry `{itemIndex}`, `{pageNumber}` (= itemIndex + 1),
`{byteStart}`, `{byteEnd}` and `{byteRange}` placeholders; Ether
substitutes integers only. Resolver `headers` may use
`{secret:name}` placeholders, substituted host-side — never put a
raw secret in a response (responses are logged). Returning zero
sources means "not available right now" and is cached briefly.

With `permissions.sources: "search"` (or `"acquire"` to open debrid
content) your resolver can ask Ether to find bytes through the
owner's indexers and debrid via the `ResolveSources` host service,
rank the candidates yourself (or in `/match`), and return a
`release` source.

Watch state and progress are keyed per playable leaf. For paged
media, store progress against the leaf the viewer is on (its index
is the natural unit); containers themselves carry no progress.

## Publishing (`present`)

Each library publishes per protocol; the owner can override your
defaults per library afterwards.

- `plex: {base: "movie"|"show"|"artist"|"photo"}` — root→show/artist,
  middle→season/album, leaf→episode/track. More than three levels
  are flattened with indexes kept (the Studio preview shows this).
- `mediaBrowser: {collectionType, itemTypes}` — Jellyfin/Emby.
  Item types: `Movie, Series, Season, Episode, MusicAlbum, Audio,
  Book, PhotoAlbum, Photo`, mapped per level; unmapped levels use
  the collection's natural container.
- `stremio: {type}`, `xtream: {category}`, `silo: {type}`.
- `adapterOnly: true` — no generic mapping fits; ship a
  `frontend_adapter` and serve the protocol yourself. Embed
  `/ether/v1/kind-media/{itemId}` stream URLs for bytes (the SDKs'
  `StreamURL`/`stream_url`/`streamUrl` helper) instead of proxying
  media through the adapter.

A library the owner cannot see is invisible to that viewer on every
surface; you never check viewer permissions yourself.

## Matching

Matching is yours; persistence and the console are Ether's. A manual
pin from the item drawer always wins, then your best score at or
above the kind's threshold (manifest default, owner-editable), then
an inline match during resolve. Give plain-language `reasons` — the
owner reads them.

## Host services

Beyond the usual services, kind plugins get (capability-checked on
every call): `KindUpsert` / `KindDelete` (push kinds), `KindItems`
(read your own library back), `ResolveSources`, and
`CachePut` / `CacheOpen` for the per-library blob cache
(content-addressed `blob:<sha256>` refs; you never name paths).
Default cache quota is 2 GiB per library under a shared cap of
min(10 GiB, 5% of the cache disk); your `cache.maxBytes` and the
owner can override it.

## Setup

Declare `contributes.setup.steps` (any plugin kind): each step lists
settings fields and an optional test route. The console walks the
steps in a drawer; a content plugin's libraries stay hidden and sync
waits until required steps pass (the owner may skip, and sees a
setup banner instead).

## SDKs

Same contract in all three, pinned by the shared fixtures in
`sdk/conformance/kinds` (each SDK's tests replay them):

- **Go** (`sdk/go`): `Plugin.OnCatalog / OnResolve / OnMatch /
  OnFrontend / OnSetupTest`, the `CatalogProvider`, `KindResolver`,
  `KindMatcher`, `FrontendAdapter` interfaces, host kind methods on
  `Host`, and `sdk/go/kit` helpers — `scrape` (polite host-HTTP
  fetching), `archivex` (zip/cbz/epub members), `metaparse` (EPUB
  OPF, ComicInfo, ID3, FLAC), `feedparse` (RSS/Atom/JSON Feed →
  items), `hints` (typed hints/fields).
- **Python** (`sdk/python`): `CatalogProvider`, `KindResolver`,
  `KindMatcher`, `FrontendAdapter`, `SetupTester` base classes with
  `on_catalog` etc., `ctx.ether.kinds` / `.cache`, `parse_feed` and
  `archive_list` helpers.
- **TypeScript** (`sdk/typescript`): `onCatalog / onResolve /
  onMatch / onFrontend / onSetupTest`, `ctx.ether.kinds` / `.cache`,
  `parseFeed`, `archiveList`, `scrapeText/Links`.

Content plugins are usually best as `remote` (scraping wants a real
process); `hosted` works for pure-API providers — the example and
the Studio template are hosted. In hosted JS, read settings with
`ether.settings.get()` and kind services via `ether.kinds`,
`ether.sources`, `ether.cache`.

## Checking your work

- The conformance kit (`kit.CheckKindProvider`, run by Studio and
  `ether plugin check`) walks your provider offline: pagination must
  terminate, pages must fit the limit, detail must round-trip, a
  declared live search must answer, resolver sources must use known
  patterns and placeholders.
- Studio's kind preview browses your draft, shows the hierarchy and
  the per-protocol projection, and dry-runs the resolver on a real
  leaf (template expansion included) before anything is installed.
- Start from the Studio "A new library" template or copy
  `sdk/examples/kind-library`; its test is the executable version of
  this page.


### Granted local files (hosted runtime)

A resolver can return a source such as
`{"id":"local","pattern":"file","path":"/picked/library/Game.nds","mime":"application/octet-stream"}`.
This requires `folders: read` and an owner-picked, non-revoked folder grant.
Ether uses the same `validateLocalFile` and `openGrantedLocalFile` path as
Stremio `ether.file`: it rejects `..`, resolves symlinks, checks containment at
resolve time and again at open time, and opens through `os.OpenRoot`.
Remote/sidecar resolvers cannot serve host files with this pattern.

### File identification without file contents

Hosted plugins can call `ether.folders.hash(root, path)` (TypeScript SDK:
`host.folders.hash`; Go SDK: `FoldersHash`). `path` is relative to the picked
root. The service requires `folders: read` and the same live folder grant as
`folders.stat`. It refuses traversal, symlink escapes and non-regular files.
It returns `{size, modTime, crc32, md5, sha1}`: Unix seconds for `modTime`,
lowercase hexadecimal digests (CRC32 IEEE, 8 digits; MD5, 32; SHA1, 40).
No file contents cross the plugin boundary. All three hashes are computed in
one streaming pass with fixed memory. `hash` stays synchronous for files up to
256 MiB; larger files must use `hashStart(root, path)` (Go: `FoldersHashStart`).
This explicitly starts a background job and returns `{id, state, bytes}`.
Poll `hashPoll(id)` (`FoldersHashPoll`) for bytes processed and state: `running`,
`done`, `canceled`, or `error`. A done job includes `result` with the hash object;
an error includes `error`. `hashCancel(id)` (`FoldersHashCancel`) requests cancellation;
poll until terminal to observe completion. Start and poll do not return file bytes.

There is no file-size ceiling for jobs. At most one runs per plugin and two
across the process; a busy start returns an error to retry later. Starting the
same active root/path returns its existing job ID. Readers yield for 2 ms after
each 1 MiB chunk. Jobs survive the initiating call, have a 24-hour deadline,
and recheck grants and cancellation every chunk. Files changing during hashing
abort without caching. Revocation or plugin disable stops ongoing reads.

Successful digests persist in a host-owned database cache indexed by plugin,
resolved path, size and nanosecond modification time. Unchanged files reuse the
cached digest after permission and containment checks. Cache rows are removed
when the plugin is uninstalled. Only explicitly requested files are hashed.
Job status is process-local, and each plugin's terminal status is retained until
its next start; after a restart, start again to reuse any completed cached result.
SDK sidecars cannot use these hosted folder services.

### Item availability

An upsert can carry
`"unavailable":{"code":"no_verified_source","detail":"No source matched the DAT record"}`.
The code must be nonempty and at most 128 bytes; detail is optional and at most
2000 bytes. The item remains visible in browse/counts so owners can inspect the
coverage gap. Ether exposes the reason in the item drawer, marks the item
nonplayable, and never calls its resolver or opens a cached resolution while
this declaration is present. The declaration also travels in frontend item
details. The next upsert without `unavailable` clears it, even with the same
etag. This is independent of the level's `playable` capability; clearing the
reason does not grant playback to a nonplayable level.

func callNoPick(ctx context.Context, rep *Report, plug *wasm.Plugin, subPath string) {
	deadline := plugins.DeadlineFor(subPath)
	cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, deadline)
	defer cancel()
	t0 := time.Now()
	resp, _, err := plug.CallDetailed(cctx, wasm.Request{
		Method:  "POST",
		Path:    subPath,
		Headers: map[string]string{"X-Ether-Request-Id": "kit-nopick"},
	})
	dur := time.Since(t0)
	rt := RouteTiming{
		Method:     "POST",
		Route:      subPath + " (without X-Ether-Pick)",
		Status:     resp.Status,
		Duration:   dur,
		DurationMS: float64(dur.Microseconds()) / 1000.0,
		DeadlineMS: deadline.Milliseconds(),
	}
	if err != nil {
		var guestErr *wasm.Error
		if errors.As(err, &guestErr) && (guestErr.Status == wasm.StatusForbidden || guestErr.Status == wasm.StatusAborted) {
			rt.OK = true
			rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
			return
		}
		rt.Error = fmt.Sprintf("subtitle refusal failed: %v", err)
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addErr("subtitles", subPath, rt.Error)
		return
	}
	if resp.Status != 403 {
		rt.Error = "subtitle route must refuse calls without X-Ether-Pick (expected HTTP 403)"
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addErr("subtitles", subPath, rt.Error)
		return
	}

	if msg := checkErrorShape(resp.Body); msg != "" {
		rt.OK = false
		rt.Error = msg
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addErr("subtitles", subPath, msg)
		return
	}
	rt.OK = true
	rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
}

func runRouteFixture(ctx context.Context, rep *Report, plug *wasm.Plugin, fx routeFixture, host *recordingHost) {
	host.mu.Lock()
	before := host.deferred
	host.mu.Unlock()
	deadline := plugins.DeadlineFor(fx.path)
	cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, deadline)
	defer cancel()
	headers := map[string]string{
		"X-Ether-Request-Id": "kit-check",
		"X-Ether-Locale":     "en",
		"X-Ether-Deadline":   time.Now().Add(deadline).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
	}
	for k, v := range fx.headers {
		headers[k] = v
	}
	t0 := time.Now()
	resp, _, err := plug.CallDetailed(cctx, wasm.Request{
		Method:  fx.method,
		Path:    fx.path,
		Query:   fx.query,
		Headers: headers,
		Body:    fx.body,
	})
	dur := time.Since(t0)
	rt := RouteTiming{
		Method:     fx.method,
		Route:      fx.path,
		Status:     resp.Status,
		Duration:   dur,
		DurationMS: float64(dur.Microseconds()) / 1000.0,
		DeadlineMS: deadline.Milliseconds(),
		OK:         true,
	}
	host.mu.Lock()
	deferred := host.deferred > before
	host.mu.Unlock()
	if deferred {
		rt.OK = false
		rt.Skipped = true
		rt.Error = "Needs a live test: this route uses a declared network service."
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addWarn("live_test", fx.path, rt.Error)
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		rt.OK = false
		rt.Error = err.Error()
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addErr("routes", fx.path, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s failed: %v", fx.method, fx.path, err))
		return
	}
	if dur > deadline {
		rt.OK = false
		rt.Error = fmt.Sprintf("exceeded route deadline of %s (took %s)", deadline, dur)
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addErr("deadline", fx.path, rt.Error)
		return
	}
	if resp.Status >= 400 {
		if msg := checkErrorShape(resp.Body); msg != "" {
			rt.OK = false
			rt.Error = msg
			rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
			rep.addErr("error_shape", fx.path, msg)
			return
		}
		rt.OK = false
		rt.Error = fmt.Sprintf("returned error status %d", resp.Status)
		rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
		rep.addErr("routes", fx.path, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s returned status %d", fx.method, fx.path, resp.Status))
		return
	}
	if fx.validate != nil {
		if msg := fx.validate(resp); msg != "" {
			rt.OK = false
			rt.Error = msg
			rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
			rep.addErr("routes", fx.path, msg)
			return
		}
	}
	rep.Routes = append(rep.Routes, rt)
}

# Ether catalogue template

Set the repository variable `ETHER_REF` to an immutable Ether release tag or commit that includes `ether plugin check` and `ether-release-sign index -check`. The workflow installs both tools from that ref. Set the `ETHER_CATALOGUE_PRIVATE_KEY` and `ETHER_CATALOGUE_PUBLIC_KEY` repository secrets to the base64 Ed25519 signing key and corresponding public key. Keep the private key secret. Pull requests validate without access to signing secrets; pushes to `main` sign and upload `index.json` and `index.json.sig` as a workflow artifact. Publish both files together at the URL configured in Ether.

Add one reviewed YAML file per plugin under `plugins/`; `examples/` contains an illustrative file with placeholder URLs and checksums. Each version must reference a publicly downloadable `.etherpkg` and its SHA-256 digest. CI downloads every non-revoked version, verifies the digest and identity, and runs `ether plugin check` on its unpacked files. The command runs the conformance kit, including copy lint. The index compiler also validates catalogue copy. A revoked entry requires a reason; it is retained in the signed index and its packages are not executed by CI.

Review permissions for each version. A version may override the entry-level permissions using its own `permissions` field. Ether verifies that the package does not request more than the reviewed permissions before marking it verified. Never use the sample values as a real catalogue entry.

# Canada Live

Adds CPAC with English/French audio and five public Global News feeds to Live TV. The broadcasters control availability and URLs. These news and public-affairs feeds do not provide a programme guide through this plugin.

## Use

Created and verified through Studio in the 0.3.3 lab. These examples do not auto-install or change server configuration on upgrade.

From the repository root:

```sh
go run ./cmd/ether plugin check sdk/examples/canada-live
go run ./cmd/ether plugin pack -o /tmp/canada-live.etherpkg sdk/examples/canada-live
```

# `etherplugin` (Go SDK)

Go authoring package (`github.com/braedonsaunders/ether/sdk/go`) for Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

## Execution modes

1. **Native HTTP or WebSocket tunnel sidecar (`ether.runtime.kind: "remote"`)**:
   Compile a standard Go binary and call `p.Serve(ctx, etherplugin.ServeOptions{})` (or mount `p` as an `http.Handler`). Host calls go over HTTP to `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential`.
2. **Hosted WebAssembly guest**: not yet supported. Go 1.27.3 `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` emits `wasi_snapshot_preview1` imports (including `proc_exit`, `clock_time_get`, and `fd_write`), which the runtime forbids. TinyGo is not installed here, so a compatible TinyGo build has not been verified. Use a sidecar until a guest is built and tested against Ether's raw WASM ABI.

## Usage

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	etherplugin "github.com/braedonsaunders/ether/sdk/go"
)

func main() {
	p := etherplugin.New(etherplugin.Definition{
		Manifest: etherplugin.Manifest{
			ID:      "org.ether.examples.hello",
			Name:    "Hello plugin",
			Version: "0.1.0",
			Ether: &etherplugin.EtherManifestBlock{
				Protocol:     1,
				Kind:         etherplugin.KindExtension,
				Capabilities: []etherplugin.Capability{etherplugin.CapListSource, etherplugin.CapUI},
				Summary:      "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
				Runtime:      etherplugin.RuntimeDecl{Kind: "remote"},
			},
		},
		Routes: etherplugin.Routes{
			Catalog: func(ctx *etherplugin.Context, req etherplugin.CatalogRequest) (etherplugin.CatalogResponse, error) {
				return etherplugin.CatalogResponse{
					Metas: []etherplugin.CatalogItem{{
						ID:          "tt0133093",
						Type:        req.Type,
						Name:        "Hello from " + req.ID,
						ReleaseInfo: "1999",
					}},
				}, nil
			},
		},
	})

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	_ = p.Serve(ctx, etherplugin.ServeOptions{})
}
```

`go test -tags ws8b ./sdk/examples/hello/go -run TestWS8bSDKInterop`.

## Tunnel recovery

`Start(ctx, ServeOptions{Mode: "tunnel", ...})` returns after the initial
credential authentication and hello/welcome handshake; initial failures are
returned to the caller. After that, dropped connections retry serially with
jittered exponential backoff (50–100 ms initially, capped at 5–10 seconds).
Every attempt re-authenticates and repeats the handshake, with a 10-second
connection/handshake timeout. A connection stable for a minute resets backoff.

In-flight calls fail on disconnect and are not replayed. Ether runtimes resolve
the current connection for subsequent calls. `handle.Done` stays open during
recovery; cancelling `ctx` or calling `handle.Close()` stops active I/O and any
retry, closes the socket, and closes `Done`. `Close` is safe to call repeatedly.
Request cancellation stops that handler without closing the shared tunnel.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket. It needs no inbound
port. Use one when the program must reach a local network, a USB device, or an
installed tool that Ether's sandbox cannot.

Set `ETHER_URL` and pair once:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
./my-sidecar
```

The SDK exchanges the code once, saves the credential, and derives the tunnel
URL from `ETHER_URL`. Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin ›
Connect a sidecar; it is valid for 5 minutes and single use. On later restarts
the saved credential is reused, so no new code is needed.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base. The pair URL and the `ws(s)` tunnel
  URL are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else the OS user config directory
  `…/ether-plugins/<plugin id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`) as JSON with the Ether URL it belongs to. If the tunnel rejects a saved
credential, the file is deleted and startup fails with one line instead of
reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM golang:1.27 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN go build -o /out/sidecar ./cmd/sidecar

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static
COPY --from=build /out/sidecar /sidecar
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
ENTRYPOINT ["/sidecar"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "docker": "ghcr.io/you/my-sidecar:1.0.0",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link. With a Docker image
the console shows a ready `docker run` command, mounting `-v ether-<id>:/data`
so the saved credential survives a restart.

# `ether_plugin` (Python SDK)

Single-file, standard-library-only Python 3.9+ SDK for Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

## Features

- Zero external pip dependencies (`http.server`, `urllib.request`, `json`, `socket`, `base64`).
- Same declarative `plugin(manifest=..., routes=...)` router shape as `@ether/plugin-sdk` and `sdk/go`.
- Runs as an HTTP sidecar (`serve(p, mode="http")`) or an outbound WebSocket tunnel sidecar (`serve(p, mode="tunnel")`).
- Includes `RemoteHostClient` for `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential`, plus `create_test_harness`, `create_mock_host_client`, `fixtures`, and starter capability templates.

## Usage

```python
from ether_plugin import plugin, serve

hello = plugin(
    manifest={
        "id": "org.ether.examples.hello",
        "name": "Hello plugin",
        "version": "0.1.0",
        "description": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
        "types": ["movie"],
        "idPrefixes": ["tt"],
        "catalogs": [{"type": "movie", "id": "hello", "name": "Hello movies"}],
        "resources": ["catalog", "meta"],
        "ether": {
            "protocol": 1,
            "kind": "extension",
            "capabilities": ["list_source", "ui"],
            "summary": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
            "runtime": {"kind": "remote"},
        },
    },
    routes={
        "catalog": lambda req, ctx: {
            "metas": [
                {
                    "id": "tt0133093",
                    "type": req["type"],
                    "name": f"Hello from {req['id']}",
                    "releaseInfo": "1999",
                }
            ]
        },
    },
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(hello, background=False)
```

Tunnel mode makes one connection and returns when it drops. Use a process
supervisor to restart the sidecar after a disconnection.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket, so it needs no inbound
port. Pair once and the SDK saves the credential:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
python3 plugin.py
```

Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin › Connect a sidecar; it is
valid for 5 minutes and single use. `serve(plugin, mode="tunnel")` resolves the
credential in this order: an explicit credential, then the saved file, then the
pairing code (exchanged once and saved). With none it raises `CredentialError`
with one clear line.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base; the pair and `ws(s)` tunnel URLs
  are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else `~/.config/ether-plugins/<id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`). If the tunnel rejects a saved credential, the file is deleted and
`serve` raises `CredentialError` instead of reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY plugin.py ether_plugin.py manifest.json settings.schema.json ./
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
CMD ["python3", "plugin.py"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "command": "python3 plugin.py",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link.


Content-kind item dictionaries may include `unavailable: {"code": "no_verified_source",
"detail": "No verified source"}`. Ether keeps these items visible with the reason
and refuses resolution until a later upsert omits the field. `pattern: "file"`
with a `path` is reserved for hosted resolvers with `folders: read`; Python
sidecars cannot access host files or call `folders.hash`. See `docs/plugin-kinds.md`.

# `@ether/plugin-sdk` (TypeScript / JavaScript)

Authoring kit for Ether plugins targeting Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

The same `plugin({ manifest, routes })` definition runs:
- **Hosted** inside Ether's embedded QuickJS + wazero sandbox (`ether.runtime.kind: "hosted"`), bundled into a single artifact with `ether plugin pack`.
- **As a sidecar** on Node or Bun (`ether.runtime.kind: "remote"`), either serving HTTP directly (`serve(p, { mode: "http" })`) or dialing outbound over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket tunnel (`serve(p, { mode: "tunnel" })`).

Hosted plugins and Studio previews have no direct host filesystem, environment,
process or network access. QuickJS `std` and `os` modules are unavailable.
Use the permission-checked `ether` host APIs for services such as HTTP and
folders. Remote sidecars run under their own operating-system permissions and
are not covered by the hosted sandbox.

## Usage

```ts
import { plugin, serve } from "@ether/plugin-sdk";

const hello = plugin({
  manifest: {
    id: "org.ether.examples.hello",
    name: "Hello plugin",
    version: "0.1.0",
    description: "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
    types: ["movie"],
    idPrefixes: ["tt"],
    catalogs: [{ type: "movie", id: "hello", name: "Hello movies" }],
    resources: ["catalog", "meta"],
    ether: {
      protocol: 1,
      kind: "extension",
      capabilities: ["list_source", "ui"],
      summary: "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
      runtime: { kind: "hosted", entry: "plugin.ts" },
    },
  },
  routes: {
    catalog({ type, id }) {
      return {
        metas: [
          {
            id: "tt0133093",
            type,
            name: `Hello from ${id}`,
            releaseInfo: "1999",
          },
        ],
      };
    },
    meta({ type, id }) {
      return {
        meta: {
          id,
          type,
          name: `Title ${id}`,
          releaseInfo: "1999",
          description: "Sample metadata entry.",
        },
      };
    },
  },
});

export const handle = hello.handle;
export const rank_key = hello.rank_key;
export const cond_match = hello.cond_match;
export default hello;

// In a separate Node/Bun entry point: await serve(hello);
```

## Capabilities and routes

- `catalog` (`GET /catalog/{type}/{id}[/{extra}].json`)
- `meta` (`GET /meta/{type}/{id}.json`)
- `stream` (`GET /stream/{type}/{id}[/{extra}].json`) and `openStream` (`POST /ether/stream/open`)
- `subtitles` (`GET /subtitles/{type}/{id}[/{extra}].json`, requires `X-Ether-Pick` header)
- `markers` (`GET /ether/markers/{type}/{id}.json`)
- `channels` (`GET /ether/channels.json`) and `guide` (`GET /ether/guide/{channelId}.json`)
- `notify` (`POST /ether/notify`)
- `event` (`POST /ether/event`)
- `view` (`GET /ether/view/{page}`) and `action` (`POST /ether/action/{action}`)
- `tool` (`POST /ether/tool/{name}`) and `job` (`POST /ether/job/{name}`)
- `file` (`GET /ether/file/{path...}`)
- `rankKey` and `condMatch` hot-path exports (`rank_key`, `cond_match`)

Tunnel mode currently makes one connection. Use a process supervisor to
restart the sidecar after a disconnection.
